source: P9.2 (2026-11-11): float widths by value (RFC 8610 §3.3, D328), numeric controls across int and float (RFC 8610 §3.8.6, D329) and .cat of text with bytes (RFC 9165 §2.2, D330). Expectations are hand-reasoned from the RFC texts; vm-test also checks each against corpus/tools/peg-oracle.mjs.
notes: float16/float32/float64 (#7.25/26/27) are sets of values: a float matches a width when that IEEE format represents its value exactly, whatever width encodes it; NaN, the infinities and the zeros are in every width (RFC 8610 §3.3: "it does not mandate that these values also do have to be serialized as half-precision floats").

The Ruby cddl gem 0.12.14 reads float32/float64 as 'needs at least that width' (1.5 is not float32); the cddl crate 0.10.7 admits every float in every width. Both disagree with the RFC's set-of-values reading on some cases here.
Numeric controls (D329): the Ruby gem agrees on all 24 cases; the cddl crate refuses all 11 cases that should match across kinds (an int against a float controller or a float against an int one).
.cat (D330): the Ruby gem agrees except that h'01' .cat "x" also matches the text string "\u0001x"; the cddl crate refuses h'01' .cat "x" in both types.

suites.name: float widths by value (D328)
suites.cddl:
f16 = float16
f32 = float32
f64 = float64
f1632 = float16-32
f3264 = float32-64
fl = float

cases.note: 1.5 as binary16 is a binary32 value
every float is a binary64 value
1.5 as binary32 is exact in binary16
1.5 as binary64 is exact in binary16
an integer is not a float

suites.name: numeric controls across int and float (D329)
suites.cddl:
speed = number .ge 0
half = int .gt 0.5
neg = int .lt -0.5
big = float .ge 9007199254740993
bigle = float .le 9007199254740993
one = float .eq 1
onei = int .eq 1.0
frac = int .eq 1.5
nz = number .ne 0
huge = int .ge -1.8446744073709552e19
nebig = float .ne 9007199254740991

cases.note: 2^53 - 1: its key's low word is all ones

suites.name: .cat of a text and a byte string (D330)

cases.note: the result has the target's type
